name: amass
paper_title: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
authors: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV) 2019, pp. 5442-5451
license: Non-commercial scientific research licence (free registration at amass.is.tue.mpg.de); commercial use requires contacting ps-license@tue.mpg.de
notes: Unifies 15 pre-existing optical marker-based motion-capture datasets (e.g. CMU, HumanEva, TotalCapture, ACCAD, BMLmovi) into one consistent SMPL/SMPL-H parameterisation via the MoSh++ pipeline (marker-to-shape fitting). ~40 hours of mocap, 344 subjects, 11,265 motions (verified as the exact motion count via multiple secondary sources; abstract/README figures commonly round this to '~11,000'). Non-commercial licence with free registration at amass.is.tue.mpg.de; the loader/preparation code (github.com/nghorbani/amass) is MIT-licensed but the DATA itself is under the MPI-IS non-commercial research licence, and commercial use requires contacting ps-license@tue.mpg.de. IMPORTANT for this repo: AMASS contains no raw inertial sensor readings at all -- it is pure SMPL/SMPL-H pose-and-shape parameters recovered from optical mocap. Here it is used only as a source of high-fidelity body kinematics from which synthetic IMU streams are generated (e.g. via virtual sensor placement + finite-difference/simulated accelerometer-gyroscope derivation), not as a real-inertial-data source. Verified 2026-09-09.
